admission.justification: Future changes to host intake, task projection or task-status consumers must preserve this bounded authority: duplicate task truth, unsupported paused observations, reconstructed membership or conflicting status/age presentation produce incorrect task operations. The named current source assertions guard the specified facets; this is no fresh Curator execution grade. The D305 Order accent is a finite presentation exception, not conflicting native status or a second activity owner.

applicability: Canonical task-status words and marks across dashboard task surfaces, with the finite D305 Order-drawing started-accent exception.
conditions: Shared taskStatusKey/statusLabel/statusTone presentation still formats native task words and status marks; unknown activity uses the task-state word without a repeated host sentence.
Only the Order drawing’s started border/ID/meta accent follows entry.stage independently of host activity. Its dependency readiness remains a separate fact, not task stage or permission.
TaskStatusWord derives displayed event age from eventAt and its shared/local display clock; a missing/inactive clock does not invent epoch zero.
exclusions: Operational severity dots, process phases, dependency-readiness badges and review/landing verdict vocabulary are distinct domains, not task-status words.
No second served task-entry elapsed age or browser-derived lifecycle/frontier task truth.
The explicit Order-drawing started accent is not a second task-status/activity/age owner; the exception does not replace the complete SprintGraphView shared task-word/mark palette.
